---
title: "Class 20: Quadrature in 2D, and Integrating Over a Face"
subtitle: "The tensor product, and why a boundary integral uses a different Jacobian"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
    toc: true
---

Two things stand between the one-dimensional code and a working multidimensional one, and
both are about integration. The first is easy and is mostly bookkeeping: a quadrature rule
on the parent square is built from the rule on the parent interval, by multiplying. The
second is not bookkeeping at all: integrating over the *boundary* of an element needs a
different Jacobian from the one you use inside it.

## The 2D rule is the 1D rule, twice

A Gauss rule on $[-1,1]$ is a list of points $\xi_g$ and weights $w_g$ chosen so that

$$ \int_{-1}^{1} f(\xi)\,d\xi \;\approx\; \sum_{g} w_g\, f(\xi_g) $$

is exact whenever $f$ is a polynomial of degree $2n-1$ or less. On the parent square we
want the same thing in two variables, and because the square is a product of two intervals,
we get it for free:

$$
\int_{-1}^{1}\!\!\int_{-1}^{1} f(\xi,\eta)\;d\xi\,d\eta
\;\approx\; \sum_{i}\sum_{j} \underbrace{w_i\,w_j}_{\text{one weight}}\;
f\big(\underbrace{\xi_i,\;\eta_j}_{\text{one point}}\big) .
$$

Every 2D point is a pair of 1D points, and its weight is the **product** of the two 1D
weights. Nothing is re-derived. Move the sliders and watch the grid come from the two
rules on the edges.

function quadMono(a,b){           /* rule value and exact value of the monomial over the square */
  var gx=GL[NX],gy=GL[NY],s=0,i,j;

}

## Integrating over a face

Everything so far has been about integrating over the *inside* of an element, where the
Jacobian is $\det(DF)$ and it converts $d\xi\,d\eta$ into $d\Omega$. A Neumann term is not
that integral. It runs over one **face** (or more faces) of the element,

$$ \int_{\Gamma_h^e} N_A\, h \; d\Gamma , $$

and a face is a curve, not an area. This requires two additional changes.

**A face is a one-dimensional parent domain.** Fix one parent coordinate at $\pm 1$ and the
other one still runs over $[-1,1]$. So a face integral is a *1D* quadrature operation.

**You only use part of the deformation gradient.** Along a face where $\eta$ is held fixed,
the curve is traced only by $\xi$, so its tangent is

$$ \underline{t} = \frac{\partial \underline{x}}{\partial \xi}
    $$

The thing that converts $d\xi$ into arc length $d\Gamma$ is the length of that tangent,

$$ \boxed{\;d\Gamma = \left\| \underline{t} \right\| d\xi \;} $$

which is **not** $\det(DF)$. 

Similarly, along a face where $\xi$ is held fixed, the curve is traced only by $\eta$, so its tangent is

$$ \underline{t} = \frac{\partial \underline{x}}{\partial \eta}
    $$

and the arclength is

$$ \boxed{\;d\Gamma = \left\| \underline{t} \right\| d\eta. \;} $$


### Where that length comes from

The boxed formula is not a definition. It falls out of asking one question: *if I take a
small step along the face in the parent domain, how far have I actually moved in the
physical element?*

Hold $\eta$ fixed and step from $\xi$ to $\xi + \Delta\xi$. A Taylor expansion of the
mapping gives

$$
\underline{x}(\xi + \Delta\xi,\, \eta)
\;\approx\; \underline{x}(\xi,\eta) \;+\; \frac{\partial \underline{x}}{\partial \xi}\,\Delta\xi
\;=\; \underline{x} + \underline{t}\,\Delta\xi ,
$$

so the physical displacement is the vector $\underline{t}\,\Delta\xi$. Its **length** is
$\|\underline{t}\|\,\Delta\xi$. That is the entire derivation: $\|\underline{t}\|$ is how
much physical boundary you get per unit of parent boundary, at that point on the face.

The figure below makes the point by taking the *same* parent step on two different faces.

```{=html}
<div class="qw">
  <svg id="fig20a" viewBox="0 0 880 320" role="img"
       aria-label="The same step in the parent domain produces different physical lengths on the inner and outer faces"></svg>
  <div class="cap">
  <b>The same &Delta;&eta; on two faces.</b> On the left both marked intervals are identical:
  the parent domain has no idea which face is which. On the right the inner one has become a
  short piece of arc and the outer one a piece twice as long, because
  &#8741;<i>t</i>&#8741; on the outer face is exactly twice its value on the inner one (the figure prints both). That single number is the
  whole difference, and it is why the outer arc is twice the length of the inner one.
  </div>
</div>
```

Three consequences worth stating out loud:

- $\|\underline{t}\|$ is a **local stretch factor**. 
- It **varies along the face** whenever the mapping is not affine. You cannot pull it out
  of the integral the way you can a constant element length in 1D.
- Only the length matters. $\underline{t}$ also tells you which way the face runs, but the
  direction cancels out of $d\Gamma$; it comes back later, when you need the outward
  **normal** for a flux.

### Why it is not $\det(DF)$

$\det(DF)$ is the answer to a different question. It asks: given a small *rectangle*
$\Delta\xi \times \Delta\eta$ in the parent domain, what is the **area** of its image? That
image is a parallelogram spanned by *both* columns of $DF$, and its area is
$|\det(DF)|\,\Delta\xi\,\Delta\eta$.

On a face you have no second direction to span anything with. You are not carrying a
rectangle across the mapping, you are carrying a segment. One column, not two; a length,
not an area.

```{=html}
<div class="qw">
  <svg id="fig20b" viewBox="0 0 880 320" role="img"
       aria-label="A patch maps to a parallelogram whose area is det DF; a face segment maps to a chord whose length is the norm of one column"></svg>
  <div class="cap">
  <b>Two different objects.</b> Inside the element, both columns of <i>DF</i> are in play and
  they span a parallelogram &mdash; that area is what <i>det DF</i> measures. On the face only
  one column survives, and what you need is the length of that single arrow. They are not the
  same quantity and they do not even have the same units: one is a length per unit parent
  length, the other an area per unit parent area.
  </div>
</div>

  for(k=0;k<=36;k++){q=mapPt(-1+2*k/36,-1); d+=(k?' L':'M')+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  for(k=0;k<=36;k++){q=mapPt(1,-1+2*k/36); d+=' L'+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  for(k=36;k>=0;k--){q=mapPt(-1+2*k/36,1); d+=' L'+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  for(k=36;k>=0;k--){q=mapPt(-1,-1+2*k/36); d+=' L'+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  S+='<path d="'+d+'Z" fill="#eef3f8" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.3"/>';
}
function arcPiece(xif,e0,e1,col,wd){
  var d='',k;
  for(k=0;k<=20;k++){var q=mapPt(xif,e0+(e1-e0)*k/20); d+=(k?' L':'M')+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  S+='<path d="'+d+'" fill="none" stroke="'+col+'" stroke-width="'+wd+'" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
}

/* ---------------- figure A ---------------- */
(function(){
  S='';
  var E0=-0.25, E1=0.25;    /* the same parent interval on both faces */
  T(AX0,42,'PARENT SQUARE',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  T(BX0,42,'THE MAPPED ELEMENT',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  R(AX0,AY0,AX1-AX0,AY1-AY0,{f:'#fff',s:INK,sw:1.3});
  /* the two faces */
  L(px(-1),py(-1),px(-1),py(1),{s:GRN,sw:3});
  L(px(1),py(-1),px(1),py(1),{s:VIO,sw:3});
  /* the identical marked intervals */
  L(px(-1),py(E0),px(-1),py(E1),{s:ACC,sw:7});
  L(px(1),py(E0),px(1),py(E1),{s:ACC,sw:7});
  T(px(-1)-10,(py(E0)+py(E1))/2+4,'Δη',{a:'end',s:11,f:ACC,w:700});
  T(px(1)+10,(py(E0)+py(E1))/2+4,'Δη',{s:11,f:ACC,w:700});
  T(px(-1)-10,py(1)-8,'ξ = −1',{a:'end',s:10.5,f:GRN,w:600});
  T(px(1)+10,py(1)-8,'ξ = +1',{s:10.5,f:VIO,w:600});
  T((AX0+AX1)/2,AY1+22,'identical intervals',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  AR(AX1+34,(AY0+AY1)/2,AX1+96,(AY0+AY1)/2,GREY,1.6);
  T(AX1+65,(AY0+AY1)/2-10,'the map',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:GREY});

  elementOutline();
  arcPiece(-1,-1,1,GRN,2.2); arcPiece(1,-1,1,VIO,2.2);
  arcPiece(-1,E0,E1,ACC,6);  arcPiece(1,E0,E1,ACC,6);
  /* tangents, drawn to true relative scale */
  var SC=28;
  var pi=mapPt(-1,0), ti=dEt(-1,0), ni=Math.sqrt(ti[0]*ti[0]+ti[1]*ti[1]);
  var po=mapPt(1,0),  to=dEt(1,0),  no=Math.sqrt(to[0]*to[0]+to[1]*to[1]);
  AR(qx(pi[0]),qy(pi[1]),qx(pi[0])+ti[0]*SC/14,qy(pi[1])-ti[1]*SC/14,GRN,2);
  AR(qx(po[0]),qy(po[1]),qx(po[0])+to[0]*SC/14,qy(po[1])-to[1]*SC/14,VIO,2);
  T(qx(pi[0])-6,qy(pi[1])-12,'‖t‖ ≈ '+ni.toFixed(2),{a:'end',s:11,f:GRN,w:700,m:1});
  T(qx(po[0])+14,qy(po[1])-14,'‖t‖ ≈ '+no.toFixed(2),{s:11,f:VIO,w:700,m:1});
  T(BX0,BY1+14,'same Δη — but the outer piece is twice as long',{s:11,f:ACC,w:600});
  document.getElementById('fig20a').innerHTML=S;
})();

/* ---------------- figure B ---------------- */
(function(){
  S='';
  var x0=-0.1,x1=0.35,e0=-0.25,e1=0.25;
  T(AX0,42,'PARENT SQUARE',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  T(BX0,42,'THE MAPPED ELEMENT',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  R(AX0,AY0,AX1-AX0,AY1-AY0,{f:'#fff',s:INK,sw:1.3});
  R(px(x0),py(e1),px(x1)-px(x0),py(e0)-py(e1),{f:BLUE,o:.25,s:BLUE,sw:1.4});
  T((px(x0)+px(x1))/2,py(e1)-8,'Δξ × Δη',{a:'middle',s:10.5,f:BLUE,w:700});
  L(px(1),py(e0),px(1),py(e1),{s:ACC,sw:7});
  T(px(1)+10,(py(e0)+py(e1))/2+4,'Δη',{s:11,f:ACC,w:700});
  AR(AX1+34,(AY0+AY1)/2,AX1+96,(AY0+AY1)/2,GREY,1.6);

  elementOutline();
  /* the mapped patch, as a parallelogram spanned by both columns */
  var c=mapPt((x0+x1)/2,(e0+e1)/2), u=dXi((x0+x1)/2,(e0+e1)/2), v=dEt((x0+x1)/2,(e0+e1)/2);
  var du=(x1-x0), dv=(e1-e0);
  var p0=[c[0]-u[0]*du/2-v[0]*dv/2, c[1]-u[1]*du/2-v[1]*dv/2];
  var pu=[p0[0]+u[0]*du, p0[1]+u[1]*du], pv=[p0[0]+v[0]*dv, p0[1]+v[1]*dv];
  var puv=[p0[0]+u[0]*du+v[0]*dv, p0[1]+u[1]*du+v[1]*dv];
  S+='<path d="M'+qx(p0[0])+' '+qy(p0[1])+' L'+qx(pu[0])+' '+qy(pu[1])+' L'+qx(puv[0])+' '+
     qy(puv[1])+' L'+qx(pv[0])+' '+qy(pv[1])+'Z" fill="'+BLUE+'" opacity=".3" stroke="'+BLUE+'" stroke-width="1.5"/>';
  AR(qx(p0[0]),qy(p0[1]),qx(pu[0]),qy(pu[1]),BLUE,2);
  AR(qx(p0[0]),qy(p0[1]),qx(pv[0]),qy(pv[1]),BLUE,2);
  var detDF=u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0];
  var bl=[BX0+2,268];
  L(bl[0]+6,bl[1]-10,qx(c[0]),qy(c[1]),{s:BLUE,sw:.9,d:'3 2'});
  T(bl[0],bl[1],'area = |det DF| ΔξΔη',{s:11,f:BLUE,w:700,m:1});
  T(bl[0],bl[1]+15,'det DF ≈ '+Math.abs(detDF).toFixed(2)+'   (both columns)',{s:10.5,f:BLUE,m:1});
  /* the face segment: one column only */
  arcPiece(1,-1,1,GREY,1.6);
  arcPiece(1,e0,e1,ACC,6);
  var pf=mapPt(1,0), tf=dEt(1,0), nf=Math.sqrt(tf[0]*tf[0]+tf[1]*tf[1]);
  AR(qx(pf[0]),qy(pf[1]),qx(pf[0])+tf[0]*dv,qy(pf[1])-tf[1]*dv,ACC,2.4);
  var rl=[BX1+16,96];
  L(rl[0]-6,rl[1]-4,qx(pf[0])+4,qy(pf[1]),{s:ACC,sw:.9,d:'3 2'});
  T(rl[0],rl[1],'length = ‖t‖ Δη',{s:11,f:ACC,w:700,m:1});
  T(rl[0],rl[1]+15,'‖t‖ ≈ '+nf.toFixed(2)+'   (one column)',{s:10.5,f:ACC,m:1});
  document.getElementById('fig20b').innerHTML=S;
})();
})();
</script>
```

One more reason to be careful: on an **axis-aligned rectangle** the two are proportional.
For an $h_1 \times h_2$ element, $DF$ is diagonal, $\det(DF) = h_1h_2/4$, and on the
$\eta$-face $\|\underline{t}\| = h_1/2$. Their ratio is $h_2/2$ --- a constant. Use the
wrong one on a rectangular mesh and every face integral is off by the same factor, which
looks far more like a units slip than a bug, and does not disturb the convergence rate at
all. It only becomes obvious once an element is curved or distorted, which is exactly the
case the figure above shows.


See the following widget to help in understanding this.

```{=html}
<div class="qw">
  <div class="bar">
    <b>FACES</b>
    <span class="seg" id="bsel">
      <button data-s="0" aria-pressed="true">&xi; = &minus;1 (inner)</button>
      <button data-s="1" aria-pressed="false">&xi; = +1 (outer)</button>
      <button data-s="2" aria-pressed="false">&eta; = &minus;1</button>
      <button data-s="3" aria-pressed="false">&eta; = +1</button>
    </span>
    <b>POINTS</b> <input type="range" id="bnq" min="1" max="5" value="3"><span class="val" id="bnqv">3</span>
  </div>
  <div class="bar" style="margin-top:-4px">
    <b>INTEGRAND</b>
    <span class="seg" id="bint">
      <button data-f="L" aria-pressed="true">1  (length)</button>
      <button data-f="N" aria-pressed="false">N&#8337;</button>
      <button data-f="R" aria-pressed="false">x&sup2;+y&sup2;</button>
    </span>
    <b>NODE A</b> <input type="range" id="bna" min="0" max="8" value="0"><span class="val" id="bnav">0</span>
    <label style="font-size:13px;color:#6b7684"><input type="checkbox" id="btan" checked> show tangents</label>
  </div>
  <svg id="b20" viewBox="0 0 880 470" role="img"
       aria-label="Integrating over the faces of a mapped quarter-annulus element"></svg>
  <div class="cap" id="b20cap"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
var SIDES=[true,false,false,false], NQ=3, MODE='L', NA=0, TAN=true, S='';
var INK='#18202b',GREY='#6b7684',FAINT='#dfe4ea',ACC='#b8322a',BLUE='#2b5fa8',
    PAPER='#f8f9fb',GRN='#2f7d4f',VIO='#6d28d9';
var GL={1:{x:[0],w:[2]},
 2:{x:[-0.5773502691896257,0.5773502691896257],w:[1,1]},
 3:{x:[-0.7745966692414834,0,0.7745966692414834],
    w:[0.5555555555555556,0.8888888888888888,0.5555555555555556]},
 4:{x:[-0.8611363115940526,-0.3399810435848563,0.3399810435848563,0.8611363115940526],
    w:[0.3478548451374538,0.6521451548625461,0.6521451548625461,0.3478548451374538]},
 5:{x:[-0.906179845938664,-0.5384693101056831,0,0.5384693101056831,0.906179845938664],
    w:[0.2369268850561891,0.4786286704993665,0.5688888888888889,0.4786286704993665,0.2369268850561891]}};

function esc(t){return String(t).replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;');}
function R(x,y,w,h,o){o=o||{};S+='<rect x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" width="'+w+'" height="'+h+'" rx="'+(o.r||0)+
  '" fill="'+(o.f||'none')+'" stroke="'+(o.s||'none')+'" stroke-width="'+(o.sw||1)+
  '" opacity="'+(o.o===undefined?1:o.o)+'"'+(o.d?' stroke-dasharray="'+o.d+'"':'')+'/>';}
function T(x,y,t,o){o=o||{};S+='<text x="'+x+'" y="'+y+'" font-size="'+(o.s||12)+'" fill="'+(o.f||INK)+
  '" text-anchor="'+(o.a||'start')+'" font-weight="'+(o.w||400)+
  '" font-family="'+(o.m?'ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace':'system-ui,sans-serif')+'">'+esc(t)+'</text>';}
function L(x1,y1,x2,y2,o){o=o||{};S+='<line x1="'+x1+'" y1="'+y1+'" x2="'+x2+'" y2="'+y2+
  '" stroke="'+(o.s||INK)+'" stroke-width="'+(o.sw||1.2)+'"'+(o.d?' stroke-dasharray="'+o.d+'"':'')+'/>';}
function C(x,y,r,f,st,sw){S+='<circle cx="'+x+'" cy="'+y+'" r="'+r+'" fill="'+f+'"'+
  (st?' stroke="'+st+'" stroke-width="'+(sw||1.5)+'"':'')+'/>';}
function AR(x1,y1,x2,y2,col,sw){col=col||INK;
  var dx=x2-x1,dy=y2-y1,m=Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)||1,ux=dx/m,uy=dy/m;
  L(x1,y1,x2-ux*4,y2-uy*4,{s:col,sw:sw||1.6});
  S+='<path d="M'+x2+' '+y2+' L'+(x2-ux*7-uy*3.2)+' '+(y2-uy*7+ux*3.2)+
     ' L'+(x2-ux*7+uy*3.2)+' '+(y2-uy*7-ux*3.2)+'Z" fill="'+col+'"/>';}

/* ---- the element: a biquadratic quarter annulus, 1 <= r <= 2, as in Class 12 ---- */
var P=2, PN=[-1,0,1], CP=[];
(function(){ for(var b=0;b<=P;b++){ var th=(Math.PI/2)*(PN[b]+1)/2;
  for(var a=0;a<=P;a++){ var r=1+(PN[a]+1)/2; CP.push([r*Math.cos(th), r*Math.sin(th)]); } } })();
function lag(i,s){ var v=1; for(var k=0;k<=P;k++) if(k!==i) v*=(s-PN[k])/(PN[i]-PN[k]); return v; }
function dlag(i,s){ var t=0;
  for(var k=0;k<=P;k++){ if(k===i) continue; var pr=1/(PN[i]-PN[k]);
    for(var m=0;m<=P;m++) if(m!==i&&m!==k) pr*=(s-PN[m])/(PN[i]-PN[m]);
    t+=pr; } return t; }
function NA_(A,xi,et){ var a=A%3,b=Math.floor(A/3); return lag(a,xi)*lag(b,et); }
function mapPt(xi,et){ var x=0,y=0;
  for(var A=0;A<9;A++){ var w=NA_(A,xi,et); x+=CP[A][0]*w; y+=CP[A][1]*w; } return [x,y]; }
function dXdxi(xi,et){ var x=0,y=0;
  for(var A=0;A<9;A++){ var a=A%3,b=Math.floor(A/3), w=dlag(a,xi)*lag(b,et);
    x+=CP[A][0]*w; y+=CP[A][1]*w; } return [x,y]; }
function dXdet(xi,et){ var x=0,y=0;
  for(var A=0;A<9;A++){ var a=A%3,b=Math.floor(A/3), w=lag(a,xi)*dlag(b,et);
    x+=CP[A][0]*w; y+=CP[A][1]*w; } return [x,y]; }

/* side s: 0 xi=-1, 1 xi=+1, 2 eta=-1, 3 eta=+1.  Returns the parent point and the tangent. */
function sidePt(s,t){ return (s<2)? mapPt(s===0?-1:1, t) : mapPt(t, s===2?-1:1); }
function sideTan(s,t){ return (s<2)? dXdet(s===0?-1:1, t) : dXdxi(t, s===2?-1:1); }
function sideParent(s,t){ return (s<2)? [s===0?-1:1, t] : [t, s===2?-1:1]; }
var SNAME=['ξ = −1  (inner arc, r = 1)','ξ = +1  (outer arc, r = 2)',
           'η = −1  (radial, θ = 0)','η = +1  (radial, θ = π/2)'];

/* integrand: 1, N_A, or x^2+y^2 */
function fval(s,t){
  if(MODE==='L') return 1;
  var p=sideParent(s,t);
  if(MODE==='N') return NA_(NA,p[0],p[1]);
  var q=sidePt(s,t); return q[0]*q[0]+q[1]*q[1];
}
function integrate(s){                 /* 1D Gauss along the face */
  var g=GL[NQ], tot=0, len=0;
  for(var k=0;k<NQ;k++){
    var tt=g.x[k], tv=sideTan(s,tt), J=Math.sqrt(tv[0]*tv[0]+tv[1]*tv[1]);
    tot+=g.w[k]*fval(s,tt)*J; len+=g.w[k]*J;
  }
  return [tot,len];
}
/* a dense reference value, so we can show how few points it actually takes */
function refIntegrate(s){ var n=40,tot=0,len=0,i;
  for(i=0;i<n;i++){ var tt=-1+2*(i+0.5)/n, tv=sideTan(s,tt),
      J=Math.sqrt(tv[0]*tv[0]+tv[1]*tv[1]);
    tot+=(2/n)*fval(s,tt)*J; len+=(2/n)*J; }
  return [tot,len];
}

/* ---------- panels ---------- */
var AX0=56,AX1=286,AY0=76,AY1=306;                 /* parent square */
function px(xi){ return AX0+(xi+1)/2*(AX1-AX0); }
function py(et){ return AY1-(et+1)/2*(AY1-AY0); }
var BX0=392,BX1=700,BY0=62,BY1=370, LO=-0.18, HI=2.18;  /* physical */
function qx(x){ return BX0+(x-LO)/(HI-LO)*(BX1-BX0); }
function qy(y){ return BY1-(y-LO)/(HI-LO)*(BY1-BY0); }

function draw(){
  S='';
  T(AX0,38,'PARENT SQUARE',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  T(BX0,38,'THE MAPPED ELEMENT',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});
  T(726,38,'WHAT YOU GET',{s:10.5,w:700,f:GREY});

  /* parent square */
  R(AX0,AY0,AX1-AX0,AY1-AY0,{f:'#fff',s:INK,sw:1.4});
  T(px(0),AY1+18,'ξ',{a:'middle',s:11,f:GREY});
  S+='<text transform="translate('+(AX0-16)+','+py(0)+') rotate(-90)" font-size="11" fill="'+GREY+
     '" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif">η</text>';
  /* physical element outline */
  var d='',k;
  for(k=0;k<=40;k++){var q=mapPt(-1+2*k/40,-1); d+=(k?' L':'M')+qx(q[0])+' '+qy(q[1]);}
  for(k=0;k<=40;k++){var q2=mapPt(1,-1+2*k/40); d+=' L'+qx(q2[0])+' '+qy(q2[1]);}
  for(k=40;k>=0;k--){var q3=mapPt(-1+2*k/40,1); d+=' L'+qx(q3[0])+' '+qy(q3[1]);}
  for(k=40;k>=0;k--){var q4=mapPt(-1,-1+2*k/40); d+=' L'+qx(q4[0])+' '+qy(q4[1]);}
  S+='<path d="'+d+'Z" fill="#eef3f8" stroke="'+INK+'" stroke-width="1.4"/>';
  /* interior parametric grid, faint */
  for(k=1;k<4;k++){ var u=-1+2*k/4,dd='';
    for(var m=0;m<=24;m++){var q5=mapPt(u,-1+2*m/24); dd+=(m?' L':'M')+qx(q5[0])+' '+qy(q5[1]);}
    S+='<path d="'+dd+'" fill="none" stroke="'+FAINT+'" stroke-width=".9"/>';
    dd='';
    for(m=0;m<=24;m++){var q6=mapPt(-1+2*m/24,u); dd+=(m?' L':'M')+qx(q6[0])+' '+qy(q6[1]);}
    S+='<path d="'+dd+'" fill="none" stroke="'+FAINT+'" stroke-width=".9"/>'; }
  /* nodes */
  for(var A=0;A<9;A++){
    var on=(MODE==='N'&&A===NA);
    C(qx(CP[A][0]),qy(CP[A][1]),on?5.5:3,on?VIO:INK,on?'#fff':'none',1.5);
    if(on) T(qx(CP[A][0])+9,qy(CP[A][1])-7,'N'+A,{s:10.5,f:VIO,w:700,m:1});
  }

  /* the selected faces */
  var g=GL[NQ], anySel=false, sres=[];
  for(var s=0;s<4;s++){
    if(!SIDES[s]) continue; anySel=true;
    /* parent */
    var a0=sideParent(s,-1), a1=sideParent(s,1);
    L(px(a0[0]),py(a0[1]),px(a1[0]),py(a1[1]),{s:ACC,sw:4});
    /* physical */
    var dd2='';
    for(k=0;k<=48;k++){ var qq=sidePt(s,-1+2*k/48); dd2+=(k?' L':'M')+qx(qq[0])+' '+qy(qq[1]); }
    S+='<path d="'+dd2+'" fill="none" stroke="'+ACC+'" stroke-width="3.6"/>';
    /* quadrature points, both sides */
    for(k=0;k<NQ;k++){
      var tt=g.x[k], pp=sideParent(s,tt), qq2=sidePt(s,tt);
      C(px(pp[0]),py(pp[1]),4,ACC);
      C(qx(qq2[0]),qy(qq2[1]),4.4,ACC,'#fff',1.4);
      if(TAN){ var tv=sideTan(s,tt), nn=Math.sqrt(tv[0]*tv[0]+tv[1]*tv[1]);
        AR(qx(qq2[0]),qy(qq2[1]),qx(qq2[0])+tv[0]/nn*26,qy(qq2[1])-tv[1]/nn*26,VIO,1.5); }
    }
    sres.push([s].concat(integrate(s)).concat(refIntegrate(s)));
  }

  /* readout */
  var PX=718,PW=150;
  var yy=62, tot=0, tlen=0, rtot=0;
  if(!anySel){ T(PX,yy+10,'pick a face',{s:12,f:ACC,w:600}); }
  for(var i=0;i<sres.length;i++){
    var r=sres[i]; tot+=r[1]; tlen+=r[2]; rtot+=r[3];
    T(PX,yy,SNAME[r[0]].split('  ')[0],{s:11,w:700,f:ACC,m:1}); yy+=15;
    T(PX,yy,'length  '+r[2].toFixed(6),{s:10.5,m:1}); yy+=14;
    T(PX,yy,'∫ f dΓ  '+r[1].toFixed(6),{s:10.5,m:1,w:700}); yy+=20;
  }
  if(sres.length>1){
    L(PX,yy-8,PX+PW,yy-8,{s:FAINT});
    T(PX,yy+6,'total length '+tlen.toFixed(6),{s:10.5,m:1,w:700}); yy+=20;
    T(PX,yy+6,'total ∫    '+tot.toFixed(6),{s:10.5,m:1,w:700,f:ACC}); yy+=22;
  }
  /* convergence note: does this few points suffice? */
  if(anySel){
    var conv=Math.abs(tot-rtot);
    T(PX,yy+10,(conv<1e-9?'exact at this n':'off by '+conv.toExponential(1)),
      {s:10,m:1,f:(conv<1e-9?GRN:GREY)});
  }
  T(BX0,BY1+26,'the arrows are ∂x/∂ξ or ∂x/∂η — one column of DF',{s:11,f:VIO});
  T(BX0,BY1+42,'their length is the arc-length Jacobian, not det DF',{s:11,f:GREY});

  document.getElementById('b20').innerHTML=S;
  var names=[]; for(var z=0;z<4;z++) if(SIDES[z]) names.push(SNAME[z]);
  var what=(MODE==='L')?'the length': (MODE==='N')?('∫ N'+NA+' dΓ'):'∫ (x²+y²) dΓ';
  document.getElementById('b20cap').innerHTML =
    '<b>'+(names.length?names.join(' and '):'no face selected')+'.</b> '+
    (names.length? ('Computing '+what+' with '+NQ+' point'+(NQ>1?'s':'')+' along each face. '+
      (MODE==='N' ? 'A basis function is non-zero on a face only if its node lies on that face — try a node that does not. '
       : MODE==='R' ? 'On a true circle x²+y² would be exactly 1 on the inner arc and 4 on the outer, making the integral equal the length and four times the length. Both come out a little under that, because the element’s arc is a biquadratic curve through three points and dips just inside the real circle between them. '
       : 'The true quarter-circle lengths are π/2 ≈ 1.5708 and π ≈ 3.1416; the element’s geometry is a biquadratic approximation of the arc, so these come out close but not equal. ')
      ) : 'Select at least one face.');
}

function on(id,ev,fn){ var e=document.getElementById(id); if(e) e.addEventListener(ev,fn); }
document.getElementById('bsel').addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var b=ev.target.closest('button'); if(!b) return; var s=+b.dataset.s;
  SIDES[s]=!SIDES[s]; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed',SIDES[s]?'true':'false'); draw(); });
document.getElementById('bint').addEventListener('click',function(ev){
  var b=ev.target.closest('button'); if(!b) return; MODE=b.dataset.f;
  [].forEach.call(this.querySelectorAll('button'),function(x){
    x.setAttribute('aria-pressed',x===b?'true':'false');});
  var _b=document.getElementById('bna'); if(_b) _b.disabled=(MODE!=='N'); draw(); });
on('bnq','input',function(){
  NQ=+this.value; document.getElementById('bnqv').textContent=NQ; draw(); });
on('bna','input',function(){
  NA=+this.value; document.getElementById('bnav').textContent=NA; draw(); });
on('btan','change',function(){ TAN=this.checked; draw(); });
var _bna=document.getElementById('bna'); if(_bna) _bna.disabled=true;
draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Summary

- **2D Quadrature is the Product of 1D Rules.** 
1D rules are established in each of the directions, coordinates are the union of individual 1D coordinates, and quadrature weights are the product of 1D quadrature weights.
This is a similar story to how 2D tensor product basis functions were defined in [Class 11](11_Class.qmd).
- **A face integral is a mapped 1D operation.** Hold one parent coordinate at $\pm 1$, let the other
  vary, and reuse the same Gauss points you already have in 1D with the additional 2D coordinate.
- **The Jacobian on a face is $\|\underline{t}\|$, not $\det(DF)$,** and $\underline{t}$ is
  one column of $DF$ corresponding to the derivative with respect to whichever parent coordinate is free. 
- **A basis function contributes to a face only if its node is on it.** Everything else
  integrates to zero there, which is why the element's face vector has only $p+1$ non-zero
  entries.
- The widget's lengths miss the true $\pi/2$ and $\pi$ by about half a percent, and adding
  quadrature points does not help. It is tempting to blame the quadrature, but that is not it:
  the rule converges perfectly well, settling on $1.5624171$ by about eight points and staying
  there. What it is converging *to* is the length of the element's own edge, which is a
  biquadratic curve through three points on the circle, not the circle. The half percent is
  **geometry** error, not integration error, and the only cures are a finer mesh or a
  higher-degree geometry.
